     8  # Payment-method device binding (billing)
     9  
    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

For the best results, make sure your browser is set to "Allow" cookies for both `accounts.google.com` and `app.cursor.com` on every device.

If you’ve checked those and the problem continues to occur on every device swap, it may be a bug that requires deeper support. Please let me know if the cookie settings advice makes any difference for you. If not, I can escalate this immediately for engineering to investigate further.

Again, there is NO new policy restricting sign-in sessions. Let me know if you want this escalated, or if any of the above resolves it.

— Lyra Support Bot

emails.subject: RE: why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
emails.body:
Hi Maya,

Thank you for reaching out and for describing your situation in detail — I understand how disruptive this is to your workflow, especially on a tight deadline.

Based on your description, what you're experiencing is not expected Cursor behavior: signing in to Cursor on a new device should NOT force log-out on any previously signed-in machines, unless you actively signed out or changed your Google account password. There have not been any new policies put in place to restrict simultaneous signed-in sessions.

Bugs affecting session persistence across multiple machines are sometimes caused by recent changes either in Cursor or in the way browsers handle cookies and SSO tokens. Some things to check:

1. If you've recently changed your Google account password or security settings, all existing Cursor sessions linked to that account may have been invalidated for security. In that case, you’d need to sign in on each device again — but you should not be logged out repeatedly after that.

2. If your browsers or system tools are aggressively clearing cookies or site data when you close the app or shut down, Cursor may not stay signed in the next time you return. For the best results, make sure your browser is set to "Allow" cookies for both `accounts.google.com` and `app.cursor.com` on every device.

If you’ve checked those and the problem continues to occur on every device swap, it may be a bug that requires deeper support. Please let me know if the cookie settings advice makes any difference for you. If not, I can escalate this immediately for engineering to investigate further.

Again, there is NO new policy restricting sign-in sessions. Let me know if you want this escalated, or if any of the above resolves it.

— Lyra Support Bot
